q: In the Cambridge guide, what is the 'experienced curriculum'?
o: What learners actually receive from the whole school experience, planned and unplanned
why: The experienced curriculum is what learners really experience, including planned and unplanned outcomes.

q: Which describes a 'spiral approach' to learning?
o: Each stage returns to key ideas and builds on them
Teaching each topic once and never returning
why: In a spiral, learners revisit key learning areas at each stage.

q: According to Cambridge, which is more important when planning a curriculum?
why: Too much content leaves no time for deep understanding. Less can be more.

q: Who writes the schemes of work and lesson plans that make a Cambridge syllabus locally relevant?
why: Cambridge says schools must create their own schemes of work and lessons.

q: How are Cambridge examiners asked to treat spelling and grammar in subjects that are not language tests?
o: Learners are not penalised for spelling and grammar errors
why: Examiners use positive marking and do not penalise spelling and grammar except in tests of language skills.

q: Which is the correct age guidance for Cambridge Lower Secondary?
why: Lower Secondary is for ages 11 to 14.

q: Which grades does Cambridge IGCSE normally award?
why: IGCSE is graded A* to G (and 9 to 1 in some subjects and zones). O Level is A* to E.

q: What is an AS Level?
o: Half the content of an A Level, normally completed in one year
why: An AS Level contains half the content of the corresponding A Level.

q: Which statement about tiers is correct for the 2024 to 2026 IGCSE ESL (0510) syllabus used in this course?
o: It has no tiers: all candidates take the same papers
It has Core and Extended tiers
why: The 2024 to 2026 syllabus removed tiering. Check the syllabus for your exam year.

q: On the CEFR scale, which levels are described as 'independent user'?
why: A is basic, B is independent, C is proficient.

q: About how many guided learning hours are recommended for a Cambridge IGCSE subject?
why: Cambridge suggests about 130 hours per IGCSE or O Level subject.

q: Which is a problem of very short lesson periods, according to the guide?
o: Lessons can become dominated by whole-class teaching
why: There is a tendency for shorter periods to be dominated by whole-class instruction.

q: What does CLIL stand for?
why: CLIL: content and language integrated learning.

q: What did Vygotsky call the area just beyond what a learner can do alone but can do with help?
why: Teachers scaffold learning within this zone.

q: Which is NOT one of the five Cambridge learner attributes?
why: The five are confident, responsible, reflective, innovative and engaged.

q: According to the guide, how should ICT be used in the classroom?
o: To support carefully planned teaching and learning goals, not replace them
why: Technology must enhance planned goals, not replace them.

q: How many weeks should be used for new lessons in a 36 to 40 week school year?
why: Leave the last 6 to 8 weeks as an exam buffer.

q: What is a thematic module?
o: A 4 to 6 week block built around one popular topic
why: Modules group about 4 to 6 weeks around a theme such as travel or health.

q: Which column is NOT in the medium-term scheme of work described in this course?
why: The four columns are theme and timeline, language focus, exam skill focus and assessment goal.

q: Which of these is a good learning target?
o: I can write a magazine article with a clear introduction and conclusion
why: A learning target says what the student will be able to do.

q: Which CEFR range should students ideally have when starting IGCSE ESL?
why: Strong A2 to lower B1 is the suggested entry level.

q: Which is an example of a sentence mechanics problem?
why: Subject-verb agreement is part of sentence mechanics.

q: Which best describes the initial assessment?
o: A short ungraded diagnostic used to spot weaknesses early
why: It is a diagnostic tool, not graded for a report card.

q: In the 30-minute template, how long is the writing part?
why: Part 1 is 15 minutes, Part 2 writing is 15 minutes and Part 3 speaking is 5 minutes per student.

q: After the diagnostic, what should you do first?
o: Look for patterns across the class and adjust the plan
Give the same lesson to everyone
why: Results are for planning and support, not ranking.

q: In a KWL chart, what does the W column stand for?
why: K is what I know, W is what I want to know and L is what I learned.
